Subject: Urgent: Autoscaler saturation impact & joint remediation plan

Hi Chris —

Thanks for flagging the latency spikes you saw this morning. I pulled ops into the thread (Ben) and we’ve asked engineering (Neha) to triage. Short version: we observed an autoscaler saturation event affecting your reserved pool between 08:35–09:05 PT that increased tail latency for batch inference jobs.

Proposed immediate steps:
- Ben will share a package with logs and token-level latency samples within the hour.
- We will open a temporary routing rule to divert new requests to a warm standby pool while we stabilize (estimated 30–60 min).
- We’ll run a focused canary with your top 3 endpoints and share results within 2 hours.

I know this is impacting morning traffic — we’ll prioritize response and are prepared to offer a credit if the root cause is on our side. Please confirm the best phone number for a quick 15-min call (ops-only) so we can align on the immediate routing change.

Jordan Blake

Immediate actions we executed at 08:47 PT:
1) Bumped your reserved pool headroom by adding two warm standby nodes (warm-attach) to reduce queue growth.
2) Enabled short-circuit routing to a regional warm standby cluster for requests that exceeded 800ms.
3) Disabled the aggressive scale-in policy for this customer’s group to avoid churn for the next 24 hours.

I’ve attached the tarball of logs to this thread (autoscaler-logs-2026-12-08.tar.gz). We’re continuing to run canaries; I’ll post results to the Drive and ping when we have the 10-min and 30-min canary windows complete.

Ben Carter

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Chris Park <chris.park@verbena.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 08:14:08 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Autoscaler saturation impact & joint remediation plan

Chris / team —

Thanks for the patience. I did a short RCA on the incident window and here are the technical findings and the remediation path we’re committing to:

Root cause (summary):
- A recent autoscaler policy tweak intended to reduce idle cost introduced an aggressive cool-down for warm nodes when average utilization fell below 30%. During a regional backlog spike (sudden fanout of batch jobs from 08:35–08:40), the autoscaler interpreted short-term utilization oscillation as sustained low load and issued scale-in ops that removed warm nodes too quickly. The allocator then hit a headroom shortfall while nodes were warming.

Impact:
- Period: 2026-12-08T08:35:20Z — 2026-12-08T09:05:47Z
- Manifested as queued requests, elevated p95/p99 across batch endpoints, and several client timeouts for Verbena’s jobs.

Immediate mitigations (complete):
- Manual warm-attach of 2 nodes (08:47 PT) to restore headroom.
- Disabled the new aggressive cool-down policy for all reserved pools pending verification.

Near-term remediation (this week):
- Revert autoscaler change and run a controlled A/B canary across 5 low-risk customers by Dec 12.
- Add a guard that prevents scale-in when queue depth > X (configurable per customer).

Permanent fix (by end of Q1 2027):
- Autoscaler heuristic improvements: time-weighted utilization window and predictive warm-standby ramping.
- Additional observability: token-level backpressure alerts and preemptive headroom recommendations surfaced in the Console.

Evidence attached: token-latency-samples-verbena.csv (sample traces), and I linked the autoscaler event IDs in the Drive package.

Credit path / next actions:
- Jordan, I suggest we route the credit/financial discussion via DocuSign to expedite. I created a draft credit approval packet and pasted the DocuSign URL below. If Verbena approves, we can finalize quickly.
- Chris, Ben and I are available for a technical sync at 10:00 PT today or tomorrow morning — let me know which slot works.

DocuSign (credit): https://docusign.net/RED-VERB-8741-credit-approval
Drive evidence: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/VERB-8741/autoscaler-evidence

Neha Kapoor
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
